chapters.category: Ethiopic textual tradition • Modern English research translation
chapters.title: Chapter 82 — Wisdom, the Calendar and the Leaders of the Seasons
chapters.sourceNote: Translated afresh into clear modern English from the earliest primary-language witnesses responsibly available for this chapter. Surviving Aramaic wording in 4Q209 (4QEnastrb ar), fragment 28, was given priority for its fragmentary portions corresponding to the appointed times, months, signs, dominions, heads, divisions of days and names in verses 10–13. The complete Ethiopic (Geʽez) text in August Dillmann's 1851 critical edition, Liber Henoch Aethiopice, supplies the full wording and continuity of all twenty verses. The 364-day total in verse 6 is read with the chapter's repeated, fully written total in verse 11. Difficult seasonal expressions in verses 16 and 19 are retained without adding unattested details. No modern English translation was used as the translation base, and text absent from the witnesses was not supplied.

verses.text: And now, my son Methuselah, I am telling you and writing down all these things. I have disclosed everything to you and have given you all their books. Preserve, my son Methuselah, the books written by your father's hand, so that they may be given to the generations of the world.
verses.study: Enoch entrusts written revelation to Methuselah for preservation beyond one household. Faithful transmission is treated as a responsibility to future generations.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 31:19 — a written testimony is taught and preserved
2 Timothy 2:2 — entrusted teaching is passed to faithful people

verses.text: I have given wisdom to you, to your children and to those who will become your children, so that they may give this wisdom, held in their minds, to their children throughout the generations forever.
verses.study: Wisdom is not private possession. It is held inwardly and passed onward through an unbroken chain of teaching.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 6:6–7 — words are kept in the heart and taught to children
Joel 1:3 — one generation tells the next

verses.text: Those who understand it will not sleep, but will incline their ears to learn this wisdom; it will please those who eat it more than good food.
verses.study: Understanding produces alert attention. Wisdom is pictured as nourishment whose goodness surpasses ordinary food.
crossReferences: Proverbs 2:2 — the ear is inclined toward wisdom
Jeremiah 15:16 — received words become joy and delight

verses.text: Blessed are all the righteous; blessed are all who walk in the path of righteousness and have no sin like sinners in the numbering of all their days. During those days the sun travels through heaven, entering and leaving through the portals for thirty days with the leaders of thousands in the order of the stars, together with the four that are added. These divide the four parts of the year, guide them, and enter with them as four days.
verses.study: The blessing on righteous conduct stands beside an ordered reckoning of time. Moral faithfulness and attentiveness to the created order belong to one disciplined life.
crossReferences: Psalm 119:1–3 — those who walk in an upright way are blessed
Genesis 1:14 — heavenly lights mark appointed times, days and years

verses.text: Because of these four days people go astray and do not count them in the reckoning of the whole age. People are mistaken about them and do not know them accurately.
verses.study: Neglecting the four added days distorts the full reckoning. The warning values precision where the revealed order is concerned.
crossReferences: 1 Chronicles 12:32 — understanding the times guides right action
Proverbs 19:2 — haste without knowledge misses the way

verses.text: For they belong to the reckoning of the year and are truly assigned forever: one at the first portal, one at the third, one at the fourth and one at the sixth. The year is completed in 364 days.
verses.study: The four days belong within the year rather than outside it. Their fixed placement completes the chapter's 364-day scheme.
crossReferences: Genesis 8:22 — ordered seasons continue while the earth remains
Psalm 104:19 — the moon marks appointed times

verses.text: The account of them is true, and the measured reckoning is exact, because Uriel showed me the lights, the months, the festivals, the rainy seasons and the days, and breathed the knowledge over me. The Lord of all the creation of the world commanded him concerning me through the power of heaven.
verses.study: Enoch attributes the calendrical disclosure to divine command mediated by Uriel. Its purpose is careful knowledge of recurring times, not independent speculation.
crossReferences: Ecclesiastes 3:1 — every purpose has its appointed time
Daniel 8:16 — an angel is commanded to explain a vision

verses.text: He has authority in heaven over night and day, to make light appear upon humanity—the sun, the moon, the stars and all the powers of heaven that turn in their circuits.
verses.study: The heavenly lights serve humanity within an ordered authority. Their circuits display coordinated service rather than self-rule.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:16–18 — the greater and lesser lights govern day and night
Psalm 19:4–6 — the sun follows its appointed course

verses.text: This is the order of the stars that set in their places, in their appointed times, in their festivals and in their months.
verses.study: Place and time are joined in the stars' order. Their settings belong to a regular pattern of months and appointed observances.
crossReferences: Job 38:31–33 — the constellations and ordinances of heaven are governed
Psalm 74:16–17 — day, night and seasons are established

verses.text: These are the names of those who guide them, who keep watch and enter at their appointed times, according to their orders, their seasons, their months, their dominions and their stations.
verses.study: The text describes layered stewardship through named heavenly guides. Each movement is bounded by time, order, authority and place.
crossReferences: Psalm 103:20–21 — heavenly servants perform the Lord's word
Colossians 1:16 — dominions and authorities belong within created reality

verses.text: Their four leaders enter first and divide the four parts of the year. After them come twelve leaders of the orders, who divide the months and the year of 364 days, together with the leaders of thousands who distinguish the days. The four that are added to them are the leaders that distinguish the four divisions of the year.
verses.study: The calendar is presented as a hierarchy of quarters, months and days. The four added days mark the year's main divisions and preserve its total.
crossReferences: Genesis 1:14 — lights distinguish seasons, days and years
1 Corinthians 14:40 — ordered arrangement serves clarity

verses.text: These leaders of thousands stand between leader and led; one is added after each station, and their leaders make the divisions.
verses.study: Intermediate leaders connect the larger order with its individual divisions. The image emphasizes coordinated responsibility at every level.
crossReferences: Exodus 18:21–22 — ordered leaders share responsibility
Numbers 2:1–2 — the community is arranged by its appointed standards and places

verses.text: These are the names of the appointed leaders who divide the four parts of the year: Melkiel, Helemmelek, Meleyal and Narel.
verses.study: Naming the four leaders makes the seasonal divisions concrete and accountable within the vision's ordered world.
crossReferences: Psalm 147:4 — God numbers and names the stars
Isaiah 40:26 — the heavenly host is called out by name

verses.text: The names of those whom they guide are Adnarel, Iyesusael and Iylumiel. These three follow the leaders of the orders, and one follows after the three leaders of the orders that follow the leaders of the stations who divide the four parts of the year.
verses.study: The nested sequence continues from seasonal leaders to subordinate guides. The repetition underlines regular succession rather than disorder.
crossReferences: Hebrews 1:14 — heavenly spirits are sent for service
Daniel 7:10 — innumerable servants stand before the heavenly throne

verses.text: At the beginning of the year the first rises and rules: Melkiyal, whose name is called Temeani and Sun. All the days under his dominion, during which he rules, are ninety-one days.
verses.study: The first quarter begins under a named leader and spans ninety-one days. The measured term connects heavenly rule with the experienced year.
crossReferences: Psalm 90:12 — wisdom attends to the numbering of days
Ecclesiastes 3:1 — each matter has its season

verses.text: These are the signs of the days that appear upon the earth during the days of his dominion: sweat, heat and stillness. All the trees bear fruit, leaves come out on every tree, the wheat is harvested, the rose blooms, and all the flowers blossom in the open country; but the trees of the rainy season become dry.
verses.study: The first quarter is recognized by signs in bodies, fields and trees. The calendar is tied to lived changes on earth, including both fruitfulness and drying.
crossReferences: Song of Songs 2:11–13 — seasonal change appears in blossoms and fruit
Psalm 65:9–13 — the earth's growth accompanies God's ordering of the year

verses.text: These are the names of the leaders beneath them: Berkiel, Zelebsael and another leader of a thousand who is added, whose name is Heloyaseph. The days of this one's dominion are then completed.
verses.study: The close of the first dominion is marked by named subordinate leaders. Completion occurs within an assigned term.
crossReferences: Psalm 104:19–23 — appointed cycles govern work and rest
Daniel 4:17 — delegated rule remains subject to heavenly decree

verses.text: The second leader after them is Helemmelek, whose name they call Bright Sun. All the days of his light are ninety-one days.
verses.study: A second ninety-one-day term begins under Helemmelek. The title Bright Sun matches the intensified light of this seasonal division.
crossReferences: Psalm 19:5–6 — the sun's course reaches across the heavens
Ecclesiastes 1:5 — the sun rises, sets and returns to its course

verses.text: These are the signs of his days upon the earth: burning heat and dryness. The trees bring out their fruit, heated and ripe, and their fruit becomes dry. The sheep pair and become pregnant. All the fruit of the earth is gathered, along with everything in the fields, and the grapes are trodden. These things occur during the days of his dominion.
verses.study: The second division is identified by heat, ripening, reproduction and harvest. The vision links celestial reckoning to the work and provision of the land.
crossReferences: Deuteronomy 16:13 — the harvest is gathered from threshing floor and winepress
Amos 9:13 — harvest and grape treading picture the land's abundance

verses.text: These are their names, their orders and the leaders beneath these leaders of thousands: Gedaeyal, Keel and Heel. The name of the leader of a thousand added with them is Asfael. The days of his dominion are then completed.
verses.study: The chapter closes this portion of the seasonal list with names, rank and completion. Ordered time advances through appointed service toward a defined end.
crossReferences: 1 Chronicles 27:1 — divisions serve in their appointed months
Daniel 2:21 — God changes times and seasons

explanation.heading: Chapter teaching and context
paragraphs: Chapter 82 closes the Astronomical Book by turning revelation into an intergenerational trust. Enoch gives Methuselah written books and commands that their wisdom be preserved in mind and handed onward.
The chapter joins righteous living with exact attention to created order. Its 364-day scheme uses four added days to distinguish four seasonal divisions, while twelve leaders distinguish the months.
Named heavenly leaders serve within assigned stations and terms. The hierarchy does not displace the Creator; it describes ordered service under the Lord who commanded Uriel to teach Enoch.

Seasonal signs—heat, leaves, grain, flowers, fruit, conception, harvest and grape treading—connect the heavenly reckoning to ordinary life on earth. Wisdom notices both moral paths and the dependable rhythms of creation.

crossReferences: Genesis 1:14–18 — lights mark appointed times, days and years
Deuteronomy 6:6–7 — wisdom is kept in the heart and taught to children
Psalm 19:1–6 — the heavens display ordered testimony
Psalm 104:19–23 — lights govern recurring times and work
Ecclesiastes 3:1 — every matter has its season
Daniel 8:16 — an angel is commanded to explain heavenly revelation
